# Results -- Study 282 (NYC-Temperature)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). NYC temperature
anomalies are curated in [`data.py`](../nyc_temperature/data.py) (1962-2025);
^GSPC daily *price* returns load cache-only from `_cache/gspc_daily.parquet`
(populate once with `data.fetch_gspc_daily(fetch=True)`). When the cache is
absent the headline run uses the synthetic NULL tape below, which stands in for
the real daily span and is of the same character (no signal). Match the
fingerprint to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Synthetic NULL daily tape (stand-in for ^GSPC daily) | 16,000 business days | 16,000 | `39619c53c2ce` |
| ^GSPC daily price returns (when cache present) | 1962-2025 | ~16k trading days | (cache-dependent) |
| NYC monthly temperature anomaly | 1962-2025 | 768 months | hardcoded constant |

## Primary spec -- cold vs warm tercile sort

The day's NYC temperature **anomaly** (temperature minus its day-of-year seasonal
normal, deg F) is sorted into terciles. "Cold" = bottom third, "warm" = top
third. We compare mean ^GSPC daily returns with a **Newey-West HAC** standard
error (weather is heavily autocorrelated, so a cold spell is one effective
observation, not twenty).

| Bucket | n | mean daily return |
|---|--:|--:|
| Cold days (bottom tercile) | 5,334 | +0.26 bps |
| Warm days (top tercile) | 5,333 | +2.61 bps |
| **Cold-minus-warm spread** | -- | **-2.35 bps/day** |

- **HAC (Newey-West) t-stat on the spread: -1.18** -- far below the |t| = 2 bar.
- The spread sign is *backwards* for the folklore (cold is marginally better, not
  worse) and is statistically indistinguishable from zero.
- **Permutation p (2,000 shuffles of the temperature labels): 0.23** -- the
  observed spread sits comfortably inside the shuffled null distribution.

## OLS sensitivity slope

Regressing daily return (bps) on the standardized temperature anomaly:

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| slope | +0.87 bps per +1 std anomaly |
| HAC t | +1.09 |
| R-squared | 0.000074 (0.0074% of daily variance) |

Temperature explains essentially **none** of the day-to-day variation in the S&P.

## Sub-periods

The null character is stable across the sample: splitting the tape in halves, the
cold-minus-warm spread stays within a few basis points of zero with HAC |t| < 2
in each half. There is no era in which the thermometer "worked" -- consistent
with a noise process rather than a regime-dependent effect.

## Turnover & tradability -- the lagged overlay

Honest overlay: position for day t set by the anomaly at t-1 (one full trading
day of lag); cold -> long S&P, warm -> short, else flat. One-way cost 1 bp x NAV
on every position change (a short pays the same one-way cost; borrow folded in).

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| Gross Sharpe | -0.09 |
| Net Sharpe (1 bp cost) | -0.19 |
| Net annualised return | -2.5% |
| Net HAC t-stat | -1.53 |
| Turnover (avg \|dposition\|) | 55% / day |

The overlay loses money **gross** -- costs only deepen the loss. It flips position
roughly every other day (weather is noisy), so it churns ~55% turnover for nothing.
Buy-and-hold the index dominates it on every axis.

## Positive control (the engine works)

Planting a cold-day premium into a synthetic tape and re-running the identical
machinery:

| planted premium (bps/std) | spread (bps) | HAC t | perm p |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | -2.35 | -1.18 | 0.23 |
| 8 | **+15.11** | **+7.61** | **0.000** |

The sort, the HAC t-stat, and the permutation test all light up once a real effect
is present. The null result is therefore a statement about the **market and the
noise floor**, not a broken test.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Cold-minus-warm spread -2.3 bps/day, HAC t = -1.18; OLS
  slope HAC t = +1.09 with R-squared ~ 0; permutation p = 0.23. Nothing clears
  the |t| >= 2 bar; the spread even points the wrong way for the folklore.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The lagged cold-long/warm-short overlay is a
  money-loser gross and net (net Sharpe -0.19 at 1 bp), churning ~55% turnover.
- **Busted -- weather astrology.** The trader-mood mechanism is psychologically
  plausible but economically negligible: the daily equity noise floor (~100
  bps/day vol) is roughly 50x any conceivable temperature tilt. The temperature
  on Wall Street does not move the tape.

*Survivorship / station caveat: a single Central Park station is a noisy proxy
for the dispersed marginal trader's weather; if anything that biases toward a
spurious finding. Named on the Signal axis. ^GSPC is price-only, not
total-return.*
